name: Tannheim
kurzbeschreibung: The heart of the Tannheimer Tal, with the Vilsalpsee, the Neunerköpfle ski area, and breathtaking mountain scenery.
beschreibung:
Überblick

Tannheim is situated at an elevation of 1,097 meters in the district of Reutte (Außerfern), forming the vibrant core of the Tannheimer Tal, widely praised as the most beautiful high valley in Europe. Home to approximately 1,160 residents across 51.3 square kilometers, this historic alpine municipality borders directly on Bavarian Allgäu. Majestic peaks of the Tannheim Mountains and Allgäu Alps encircle the valley floor – including the Neunerköpfle, Einstein, Aggenstein, and the legendary rock climbing peaks Rote Flüh and Gimpel. Encompassing traditional hamlets such as Berg, Bogen, Innergschwend, and Kienzen, Tannheim enjoys worldwide acclaim among hikers, mountaineers, paragliding pilots, and Nordic skiers throughout all seasons.

Geschichte

Early records of the valley date back to around 1100, noted in the endowment records of the Swabian monastery Ochsenhausen. Permanent settlement developed from the 13th century onward through Alemannic settlers arriving across the passes from the neighboring Ostrachtal. The village was first documented in 1342 under the name Tanhain. In 1416 Duke Frederick IV of Austria confirmed the valley's historic privileges, and in 1464 Tannheim was designated the local seat of justice. A crowning achievement of regional sacred architecture is the parish church of Saint Nicholas. After a lightning strike damaged the Gothic predecessor, local master builder Andreas Hafenegger from Haldensee erected the current monumental Baroque church between 1722 and 1725, drawing inspiration from St. Jakob's Cathedral in Innsbruck. It is the second largest rural parish church in the Diocese of Innsbruck and features a historic carillon cast by Gregor Löffler in 1561. Another precious landmark is Felixé Mina's Haus: built in 1698 and inhabited by the prominent Zobl family, it has been meticulously restored as a living folk museum and cultural hub. The pristine Vilsalpsee was designated a nature reserve as early as 1957.

Anreise

Tannheim boasts superb accessibility and can be reached from Germany completely toll-free. Drivers traveling from Germany follow the A7 motorway to the Oy-Mittelberg exit and continue via Wertach and the Oberjoch Pass along the B199 Tannheimer Straße directly into the valley. From the Tyrolean Inntal, travelers journey via the Fern Pass (B179) to Reutte and cross the Gaicht Pass into Tannheim. Rail travelers utilize convenient railway stations at Sonthofen (Bavaria, approx. 24 km), Pfronten-Ried, or Reutte in Tirol. From these stations, VVT regional bus line 120 and Allgäu public buses provide reliable transfers. Within the valley, guest card holders travel free on local hiking and ski shuttles.

Tipps

A quintessential excursion is visiting the protected Vilsalpsee nature reserve at 1,165 meters. This emerald-green mountain lake, embraced by precipitous cliffs, features an easy 4.5-kilometer lakeside loop trail; to preserve the delicate ecosystem, daytime motor vehicle access is restricted, inviting visitors to arrive on foot, by horse-drawn carriage, or aboard the red tourist train Tannheimer Alpen-Express. The local cable car whisks adventurers up to the Neunerköpfle (1,862 m), home to the famous Largest Summit Book in the Alps measuring nearly three meters tall, alongside the interactive 9erlebnisweg themed trail. The summit is also a premier global launch site for paragliders. Culture lovers should tour Felixé Mina's Haus in the village center to discover authentic domestic life spanning three centuries.
